newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - Nov 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - Nov 3.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TIMES
-- BT AND MCI MERGE INTO CONCERT

British Telecom and MCI will announce terms for a merger today. The deal will involve BT buying the 80 per cent of MCI that it does not already own for 12 billion pounds stg. The offer will value MCI, America's second-largest long-distance phone company, at around 15 billion pounds stg or 36 dollars US a share. The merger will create a new holding company to be called Concert, the name of the two groups' existing joint venture in corporate network management.
-- BANK WANTS MORE RISES IN INTEREST RATES

The Bank of England believe that Britain's recent inflation performance has been disappointing and that there should be a bias towards a further tightening of monetary policy following last week's base rate rise from 5.75 per cent to 6 per cent. The analysis to be published in its inflation report on Wednesday is unlikely to call for an immediate rise but will point to the increases if the government wants to ensure it meets its 2.5 per cent inflation target.
-- CAMELOT AIMS TO GO GLOBAL

The national lottery operator, Camelot, is planning to expand overseas, setting up a separate international arm to run foreign lotteries. The move would secure the future of Camelot beyond 2001, when its UK licence expires, and smooth the way for a potential stock-market float.
-- GENERALE SEEKS TO SELL 500 MILLION POUNDS HEALTHCARE ARM

Generale Des Eaux, the French utilities giant, is believed to have put up for sale BMI, Britain's second-largest private healthcare provider. It is thought that as well as buyers being sounded out, executives at BMI are exploring management buyouts of parts of the organisation.
-- THREE OIL GROUPS PLAN FILLING STATION MERGER

Gulf, Elf and Murco, three of Britain's biggest petrol station owners are thought to be in talks to merge forecourt and refining operations, to create the UK's fourth biggest petrol station group after Esso, Shell and BP. The talks are intended to counter the growing competition from supermarket groups and the petrol pump price war.
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- LABOUR WILL CLIP BANK GOVERNOR'S WINGS

The Labour party is proposing to scrap the personalised meetings between the chancellor and the Bank of England governor. Gordon Brown, the shadow chancellor is proposing to replace it with a Monetary Policy Committee to provide him with advice on interest rates and the economy.
-- RANK FACES BIG PROPERTY HIT

Rank, the leisure group, is carrying out a wide-ranging revaluation of all its properties . The move could lead to a writedown of up to 300 million pounds stg at the year's end, wiping out much of the group's profits, City analysts said. Rank also want to raise 900 million pounds stg by selling off many of its freehold properties to City institutions and leasing them back.
-- McCORMACK AND SOROS EYE CHELSEA

A list of potential investors in Chelsea Village, the owners of Chelsea Football Club are waiting to see the outcome of the stake owned by Matthew Harding's family estates. Matthew Harding who owned 25 per cent of the club, was killed in a Helicopter crash last week. The list of speculators includes George Soros, Granada, Mark McCormack's IMG, Guinness Peat Group and the McCarthy Corporation.
-- UNIPART ON TRACK FOR RAILPART

Unipart, the automotive parts manufacturer and distributor is one of the four shortlisted bidders for Railpart, the rail components and spare parts distributor, which is expected to be sold for up to 100 million pounds stg by the end of the year.
-- UPS PREPARES CHARTER ASSAULT

United Parcel Service, one of the world's leading package delivery companies looks set to move in on the European and American passenger charter flight market. It plans to convert five of its 51-strong fleet of Boeing 727-100s into quick-change freight-to-passenger aircraft in a bid to increase use.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- FACIA BANK SUES OVER LOAN DEALS

United Mirzrahi Bank, the main backer of Stephen Hinchliffe's Facia group, is suing the former head of its London branch, Rafael Kellner and John Doherty, its former head of lending, for allegedly taking backhanders for arranging loans of more than 8 million pounds stg to the collapsed retailer.
-- BT WILL SELL MURDOCH STAKE

BT is ready to sell the 13.5 per cent stake in Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation it will inherit from MCI as part of the planned merger to stave off opposition from the regulators. BT is determined that possible conflicts from its direct shareholding in News Corporation will not stand in the way of the deal.
-- MORGAN PLANS MARKET RETURN

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell looks set to re-enter the UK equity market eight years after it withdrew from the London market, sacking 450 staff. DMG will activate its Stock Exchange membership next week as a precursor to full scale trading in London equities.
-- LAST-MINUTE BID DUE FOR LLOYDS

The City is readying itself for a last minute rival bid for Lloyds Chemists from Gehe of German. The Takeover Panel deadline expires on Friday. Gehe has been biding its time following Unichem's 657.6 million pounds renewed cash and share offer two weeks ago, but looks set according to sources to be ready to make a renewed offer.
-- OFLOT EYE ON CAMELOT EXPANSION PLANS

Camelot, the national Lottery operator is being investigated by its regulator, Oflot, over plans for an international expansion that could put it in breach of its licence. Camelot have been asked for reassurances that a new offshoot called Camelot International Services will not breach of the company's license provisions.
OBSERVER
-- BA PUTS DOMESTIC ROUTES UNDER FIRE

British Airways is poised to axe domestic routes to Belfast, Newcastle and Plymouth if it has to surrender take-off slots at Heathrow as a condition of its proposed deal with American Airlines. The vulnerable regional services have been put on the block as negotiations with the competition authorities and the government reach there final stage this week.
-- TREASURY PLANS NEW MOVE ON SOCIETIES LAW

The Treasury may propose new legislation aimed at preserving building societies next month. Some societies are believed to be expressing concern to the government that they are vulnerable to the Alliance & Leicester's expansion plans, that include takeovers after it joins the stockmarket, and may launch a rights issue.
-- KINGFISHER MEASURES UP FRENCH DIY DEAL

Kingfisher, the British retail combine is considering plans for a major move into the French DIY industry. They are hoping to strike a deal to take a stake in one of France's two largest DIY Retailers, Leroy Merlin or Castorama, but the move is not likely to take place until next summer.
-- NORTHERN SEES WHITE KNIGHT IN ENTERGY

Entergy, the US power company, is thought to be planning a move to rescue Northern Electric, which is facing a 766 million hostile bid from US independent power producer CalEnergy. A spokesman for Entergy said that they could not confirm or deny the story, but confirmed that they see the UK as a favorable market to pursue.
-- KWIK SAVE TO SHED STORES AND STAFF AS PROFITS DROP

Kwik Save, the discount food retailer, will announce next week a shake-up that will involve the closure of stores and major job losses. The retailer has close to 1,000 outlets and it is thought that at least 100 will close with some estimates being nearer to 300. The move follows a sharp fall in profits and a collapse in its share price.
-- MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- VIRGIN SPREADS ITS EURO WINGS

Richard Branson's Virgin Express is expected to put in a bid tomorrow for Air Liberte. The move will challenge British Airways for the ownership of the bankrupt French airline which has about 12 per cent of the French domestic market. BA have already offered 98 million stg to the administrators.
-- LABOUR WINDFALL TAX FACES COURT BATTLES

There are growing doubts over Labour's ability to levy its much publicised 5 billion stg windfall tax on the privatised utilities. Experts are predicting that Tony Blair will have to head-off legal challenges over the tax in the European and domestic courts if he wins the next election.
-- PARTNERS IN BIOTECH BOOM

The Medical Research Council is set to join the City's biotech boom. The MRC plan to launch a venture capital fund in the New Year. The new fund, UK Medical Ventures, thought to be the first time a government agency has established a venture capital fund, hopes to attract up to 35 million pounds stg to invest in MRC backed discoveries.
-- SKIPTON FACES WRIT FOR 250,000 POUNDS DAMAGES

First Mortgage Group is serving a writ against the Skipton Building Society, Britain's 13th largest, for losses allegedly suffered through its dealings with Skipton's mortgage administration subsidiary, Homeloan Management and follows similar writs issued by Lloyds, Abbey Life and Axa Equity & Law.
-- SAINSBURY SET TO GO SHOPPING

Sainsbury are considering bidding for smaller grocery businesses in its fight to regain market share. According to new chief executive Dino Adriano, the company is particularly keen to increase its representation in the North, Wales and the west of England and Scotland. Increasingly tight planning regulation may mean that corporate acquisitions become the easiest way to buy out-of-town sites.
